transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-19 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CSM) -- Jordan Lee (Atlas Head Eng), Priya Desai (InfoSec), Marco Ruiz (Procurement), Ellen Park (Cloud Arch)

Summary: Quick procurement + legal handoff; focus on MSA/DPA redlines, billing appendix, SLA objectives, and a small benchmark to unblock pricing commit. Some noise on acronyms and a couple of transcription hiccups (K V cache, KMS/H S M).

Topics: MSA redlines, DPA exceptions, billing cadence, SLA targets (p95/p99), private deployment vs hosted, KMS integration, audit logs and retention, procurement PO path, next steps for legal/finance sign-off.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for carving time today. i think this is the procurement / commercial handoff — we'll run through the redline status, the billing appendix and then samir will outline the perf bench we recommended.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: yep, thanks Maya. quick thing — Finance wanted to see a definitive SLA at p99 for our latency sensitive flows, and also the billing appendix must show line items for reserved capacity vs on-demand.
[00:32] Marco Ruiz: and just to add, procurement needs to know if you accept PO before contract signature or invoice-only. last time we had to route through our AP team it got delayed.
[00:45] Maya Chen: totally, that's helpful. on the PO question we usually accept PO with net-30 for enterprise but we can also do invoice-only for pilot. we'll put both options in the appendix, with the default being invoice on host for early pilot.
[01:02] Priya Desai: on the security side, we need explicit KMS/HSM notes, SSO SAML integration details, and audit log retention — minimum seven years for certain regulated data. are those in scope?
[01:18] Samir Patel: yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS, and HSM-backed key storage for private deployments. quick caveat: for hosted API we use envelope encryption and a KMS integration pattern — there are some subtle differences in the rotation process. samir pause — sorry, that came out kinda technical.
[01:35] Ellen Park: can you clarify the difference between hosted with customer KMS and dedicated private? like network egress and whether data ever leaves our VPC.
[01:48] Samir Patel: right, so hosted with customer KMS still routes through Redwood control plane and there is encrypted transit to the serving plane; with Private/VPC we deploy the serving plane in your VPC so data does not traverse public internet. sometimes transcript shows K V cache oddly as K V cache, but we mean KV cache for inference state.
[02:08] Jordan Lee: okay, that's important. our legal team will want the VPC deployment described clearly with diagram.
[02:15] Maya Chen: we'll attach a network diagram to the redline. on the SLA numbers — you mentioned p99. for workloads with 512 token tails we have two profiles: hosted optimized and dedicated reserved. dedicated tends to hit p99 under 300ms in our benchmarks, hosted can be as low as 250ms but depends on burst.
[02:39] Marco Ruiz: sounds like cost tradeoffs will matter. procurement needs a deterministic pricing model when we go to commit. can you outline reserved capacity discounts and how overage is billed?
[02:52] Samir Patel: yes — reserved capacity is a monthly commitment with steeper discounts; overage is billed at an on-demand rate with clear thresholds. we'll add a worked example in the appendix: commit for 4 GPUs, baseline throughput X, overage Y per token.
[03:08] Jordan Lee: oh and one more thing, do you support token-based metering with server-side traces, because our finance needs an exportable usage CSV per project?
[03:19] Lena Ortiz: we provide per-token and per-embedding usage exports, plus token-level breakdowns in the console. we can push a sample CSV.
[03:27] Priya Desai: regarding audit logs, our compliance requires immutability and retention controls. do you have WORM or append-only logs?
[03:38] Samir Patel: currently audit logs are immutable in our host, with export to your S3 if needed. for Private we can configure log sinks into your audit pipeline. we'll note the retention windows and support for compliance exports.
[03:51] Marco Ruiz: procurement will want to see SLA credits language — is there a standard remedy or do you provide remedies + termination thresholds?
[04:00] Maya Chen: our standard MSA has a credits-based remedy tied to availability SLOs; termination for repeated breaches is negotiable. we'll mark the clause and propose a governance schedule for escalations.
[04:13] Jordan Lee: legal will push on the DPA: specifically subprocessor list and data residency. do you maintain subprocessors for model hosting?
[04:23] Samir Patel: we do; models run on our serving fleet and we list cloud providers as subprocessors. we can provide the subprocessor list and a commitment to notify of changes. also note that model weights for certain open models are pulled from mirrors — we can include that in the appendix.
[04:40] Ellen Park: about benchmarks — can you replicate our real workload? we have lots of short prompts, high concurrency, with an embedding pipeline that hits 10k qps.
[04:52] Samir Patel: we can run a benchmark with your sample traffic profile. our plan is a two-hour run to get p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-1000-token estimates. want to confirm we'll get the sample traffic and sample prompts?
[05:05] Jordan Lee: yes, Ellen will share a sanitized traffic profile and a set of prompts.
[05:09] Ellen Park: I'll upload to the secure bucket and share access.
[05:14] Priya Desai: small red flag — we need to ensure data used in bench doesn't include PII; I'll scrub before sharing.
[05:20] Marco Ruiz: budgeting question: if we sign reserved capacity, what's the minimum term? and if we want to scale down mid-term how does that affect billing?
[05:32] Maya Chen: minimum terms are usually 12 months for reserved contracts with pro rata scaling windows at quarter boundaries. we can negotiate different terms for pilot-to-production transitions. we'll call out prorated adjustments in the appendix.
[05:44] Jordan Lee: okay. procurement also asked whether Redwood will accept our standard redline for indemnity and IP — can you take a preview now?
[05:53] Maya Chen: we looked through your key points; indemnity has a few exceptions — we'll propose language that aligns with Redwood risk team but it's often a back-and-forth. we'll highlight sections that are non-starters and propose alternative language.
[06:05] Samir Patel: technical deep dive aside, one thing to watch: quantization and model variants affect latency/cost — dedicated hardware plus lower-precision variants give you better unit economics but may change output characteristics. we should tie those recommendations to the eval set so quality regressions are monitored.
[06:24] Priya Desai: good, we want to avoid silent quality regressions. a monthly or per-rollout eval policy is ideal.
[06:32] Maya Chen: Redwood Optimize can run continuous evals and alert on quality drift. we'll include an eval schedule proposal.
[06:39] Marco Ruiz: on procurement timing — what's a realistic timeline from legal sign-off to production?
[06:46] Maya Chen: from signature to private or dedicated deployment typically 4-6 weeks if there's no major network or compliance blockers; hosted API can be immediate. provisioning reserved pools maybe 2-3 weeks depending on availability.
[06:58] Jordan Lee: finance also wants a clause about price increases mid-term — do you guarantee no increases outside of indexation?
[07:06] Maya Chen: we can add a price protection clause for the first 12 months post-signature, and then indexation rules after that. we'll surface that in the appendix.
[07:16] Priya Desai: another security ask — will Redwood submit to a vendor security assessment or questionnaire? we have a standard SIG template.
[07:24] Lena Ortiz: yes, we do vendor security assessments; we can either fill out your SIG questionnaire or provide our security pack including SOC 2 report, pen test summary, and ISO attestation.
[07:35] Marco Ruiz: perfect. procurement also needs contact info for escalation: who to call for billing disputes?
[07:41] Maya Chen: i'll list billing, support, and SE escalation contacts in the redline docs.
[07:47] Jordan Lee: what about data deletion and post-term data handling? that was contentious with another vendor.
[07:54] Samir Patel: standard is data deletion within 30 days post-contract, with preserved audit logs per the retention window if requested. Private deployments can even set shorter windows. we'll make this explicit.
[08:06] Ellen Park: are there limits on entitlements per customer org? like number of teams/projects?
[08:12] Lena Ortiz: entitlements are configurable; our console supports project-level allocation and cost centers. we can map to your org structure.
[08:21] Marco Ruiz: procurement will need to see a sample invoice and a billing timeline.
[08:26] Maya Chen: yes we'll attach sample invoice and show line items: reserved monthly fee, overage, data storage, and eval hours.
[08:34] Jordan Lee: final point — competition. finance asked if you have exclusivity concerns or if you work with other financial firms.
[08:41] Maya Chen: we don't require exclusivity; we do have other financial customers but we keep data wholly separate and enforce tenant isolation.
[08:49] Priya Desai: please include tenant isolation and network segmentation details in the security addendum.
[08:55] Samir Patel: will do.
[09:00] Maya Chen: alright let's recap the concrete things we'll deliver: the redlined MSA + DPA with billing appendix and escalation contacts, the perf bench results, SOC 2 + ISO docs, sample invoice, and the network diagram.
[09:13] Jordan Lee: sounds good. procurement will get back on PO cadence.
[09:18] Marco Ruiz: i'll confirm the internal PO flow by March 23.
[09:22] Priya Desai: i'll scrub and deliver the traffic profile and required audit items by March 25.
[09:29] Ellen Park: i'll share access to the sanitized s3 bucket by end of day tomorrow.
[09:33] Samir Patel: i'll schedule the benchmark and share the sheet by the 26th.
[09:37] Maya Chen: perfect. we'll tentatively schedule a 30-minute legal/finance wrap on 2026-03-30; lena will send the invite.
[09:46] Lena Ortiz: invite will go out after the redline is uploaded.
[09:50] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity — we'll follow up with the redline and artifacts.

Recap / Next steps (verbatim):
- Maya to send updated MSA + DPA redline that reflects billing appendix (due 2026-03-24)
- Samir to run 2-hr perf bench and share cost/latency spreadsheet (due 2026-03-26)
- Marco confirm PO process (due 2026-03-23)

End of transcript.
